Sensitivity Analysis for Sample Size Planning From the AIPE Perspective for a Polynomial Change Parameter

Source: R/ss_aipe_pcm_sensitivity.R
ss_aipe_pcm_sensitivity.Rd

Quantifies how much misspecification of the population between-subject slope variance and within-subject error variance distorts an AIPE-based sample size plan for the group-by-time polynomial change parameter. On each replication the function simulates two independent groups of n subjects each, measured at \(M = f \times D + 1\) timepoints, where every subject has a true linear slope drawn from a normal distribution with mean 0 and variance true_var_trend, and within-subject observations have residual variance true_var_error. Subject-level OLS slopes are computed in each group, the between-group difference in mean slopes (the change parameter \(\beta_{m1}\) that ss_aipe_pcm plans for) is estimated, and a two-group t-confidence interval on that difference (pooled standard error, \(2n - 2\) degrees of freedom) is recorded. The function only handles trend = "linear" in the simulator; for quadratic / cubic trends, the planner's closed-form solution is still available via ss_aipe_pcm.

Usage

ss_aipe_pcm_sensitivity(
  true_var_trend = NULL,
  true_var_error = NULL,
  supposed_var_trend = NULL,
  supposed_var_error = NULL,
  duration,
  frequency,
  width,
  specified_n_per_group = NULL,
  conf_level = 0.95,
  assurance = NULL,
  G = 1000,
  print_iter = FALSE,
  filename = NULL,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

true_var_trend

Population between-subject variance of the polynomial change coefficient (the data generating \(\sigma^2_{\upsilon_m}\) of Kelley & Rausch, 2011).

true_var_error

Population within-subject error variance (\(\sigma^2_\epsilon\)).

supposed_var_trend

Planning value of true_var_trend passed to ss_aipe_pcm; supply this and supposed_var_error, or supply specified_n_per_group.

supposed_var_error

Planning value of true_var_error passed to ss_aipe_pcm.

duration

Study duration (in time units).

frequency

Number of measurements per unit time. The number of measurement occasions is \(f \times D + 1\) (the row n_occasions).

width

Desired full width of the CI on the between-group difference in change parameters (\(\beta_{m1}\)).

specified_n_per_group

Number of subjects per group to evaluate (incompatible with the supposed-variance arguments).

conf_level

Confidence level (default 0.95).

assurance

Optional assurance probability passed to the planner.

G

Number of Monte Carlo replications.

print_iter

Logical.

filename

Optional path to a CSV file; when supplied, the per-replication results (the slope difference, its interval limits and width, and the two tail misses) are written there, appended when the file already exists, and a throwaway run should point it at tempfile(fileext = ".csv"); the default NULL writes nothing.

seed

NULL (the default) to draw from the current random number stream, or a single number that makes the call reproducible; a supplied seed is set for this call only, and the caller's random number state is restored when the function returns.

Value

A data.frame with rows for mean / median / SD of the realized estimated slope difference and CI width, the proportion of intervals at or below width, tail-specific and overall non-coverage of the population slope difference (0 by construction in this simulator), and the input echoes, including assurance (present only when an assurance was supplied).

The record of the simulation

Every sensitivity function of the package summarizes its replications over one denominator: the replications that produced a confidence interval (for a power sensitivity function, a test). The proportion of intervals that met the width target (pct_ci_less_width), the proportions of intervals that missed the true value, and the summaries of the widths are all taken over those replications. A replication without an interval is in none of these rows. It is counted, and the returned table carries the counts in its attribute simulation, a list read with attr(x, "simulation"):

attempted

the number of replications asked for (G).

returned

the number that produced an interval (a test).

failed

the number that did not (attempted - returned).

denominator

the number of replications the rows named above are taken over, which is returned.

width_target_probability

the proportion of the replications with an interval whose interval met the width target, the value of the pct_ci_less_width row; NA for a function or a call without a width target, and when no replication produced an interval.

width_target_mc_ci

the exact binomial (Clopper-Pearson) limits for that proportion, at the confidence level of the table. They describe the error of the simulation, which shrinks as G grows, and nothing else.

A function that records more about its run adds elements to the list, and its help page names them. The line "Replications" beneath the printed table gives G, and the three counts when a replication was without an interval. With many replications without an interval the rows describe only the studies in which the interval could be formed, so failed is to be reported beside them.

References

Kelley, K., & Rausch, J. R. (2011). Sample size planning for longitudinal models: Accuracy in parameter estimation for polynomial change parameters. Psychological Methods, 16(4), 391–405. doi:10.1037/a0023352

Maxwell, S. E., Delaney, H. D., & Kelley, K. (2027). Designing experiments and analyzing data: A model comparison perspective (4th ed.). Routledge. (See Chapters 11 and 15.)

Examples

# Every replication simulates two full groups of subjects, fits a slope
# for each subject, and forms a confidence interval on the difference in
# mean slopes. G = 10 keeps the example quick; a reported sensitivity
# study deserves the default G = 1000. With the planning values equal to
# the population values, the realized mean width should sit close to
# the target.
set.seed(113)
ss_aipe_pcm_sensitivity(
  true_var_trend = 0.003, true_var_error = 0.0262,
  supposed_var_trend = 0.003, supposed_var_error = 0.0262,
  duration = 4, frequency = 1, width = 0.05,
  G = 10, print_iter = FALSE
)
#>  term               value
#>  mean_slope_diff    0.004
#>  median_slope_diff  0.002
#>  sd_slope_diff      0.012
#>  mean_ci_width      0.051
#>  median_ci_width    0.051
#>  sd_ci_width        0.003
#>  pct_ci_less_width  0.500
#>  pct_ci_miss_low    0.100
#>  pct_ci_miss_high   0.000
#>  total_type_I_error 0.100
#>  n_per_group        71   
#>  n_occasions        5    
#>  true_var_trend     0.003
#>  true_var_error     0.026
#>  supposed_var_trend 0.003
#>  supposed_var_error 0.026
#>  duration           4    
#>  frequency          1    
#>  width              0.050
#>  conf_level         0.950
#>
